changes.before: Change only the assigned position from at(1) to at(2). What happens to the printed second value and size?
changes.after: Store a fixed number of values in std::array.

before: std::array<int, 3> stores exactly three integers. Both the element type and the length are part of its type.
Writing values.at(1) replaces the second element. It does not add a fourth slot or change size().
The brace initializer supplies the starting values. Unlike vector, this container has no push_back operation to grow it.
at reports an invalid position instead of silently granting another slot. This example uses only positions known to be in bounds.
Expected output or behavior: 9 3. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare replacing a slot with attempting to grow the container. Explain when a fixed size is useful. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: std::array<int, 3> holds exactly three integers. Include <array> to use it. The item type and the number of items are both part of the array's type.
values.at(1) selects the second item because positions start at zero. Assigning to it replaces that item. It does not add another position.
The values inside the braces give the array its starting contents. std::array has no push_back operation because its size cannot grow.
at checks whether a position exists. An invalid position throws an exception instead of creating a new item. This example uses valid positions only.
The program prints 9 3. The second item changes from four to nine. The array still contains three items.
The array's size stays fixed for its whole life. Its items can still change unless the array is const.

before.question: Change only the assigned position from at(1) to at(2). What happens to the printed second value and size?
choices: They become 4 and 3, because only the third slot changed.
The array shrinks to two elements.
before.explanation: The assignment targets the third slot; the second remains 4 and fixed size stays 3.

after.question: Change only the assignment to values.at(2) = 9. Keep the output unchanged. What prints?
choices: The array shrinks to two items.
after.explanation: The third item changes. The output still reads the second item, four, and the size stays three.
